newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Albanian rebels roll big guns into southern town.
newsitem.headline: Albanian rebels roll big guns into southern town.

text.p: Anti-government groups took firm control of the southern Albanian town of Tepelene on Thursday, rolling big guns into the central square, a Reuter reporter said.

Men and youths, many in masks, had taken guns seized from an army barracks and hundreds were parading through the town firing into the air and controlling all entrances to the town, littered with wrecks of cars and army vehicles.
Women and children were removing virtually all other items from the building, mainly clothing and blankets, he said.
Huge stocks of dynamite -- several tonnes -- were piled in a depot inside the barracks.
The official ATA news agency said the death toll in the disturbances had risen to 25 people in the Adriatic port of Vlore, where the latest wave of violence erupted last week.
It said seven people had died since Wednesday and reported one death in Tepelene, saying a gun had gone off when rebels posed for television cameras.
Albania's army is meeting determined resistance as it pushes through volatile southern regions under state of emergency regulations passed by parliament last weekend.

But President Sali Berisha, re-elected to a second five-year term by parliament this week, told Italian Foreign Minister Lamberto Dini he would use negotiation, rather than force, to restore order in the region,

In Tirana, a justice ministry official said the head of the opposition socialist party, Fatos Nano, had been moved to the capital from Tepelene prison, where he had been held since 1994. He said Nano was moved after fighting broke out among inmates around February 23.
Small children were seen sifting through the jail picking through whatever debris they could find.
Former army officers in Tepelene were taking inventories of weapons and marshalling young rebels. They vowed to remain in place until Berisha resigned.
"We will not return our weapons until Berisha resigns," said one colonel.

"The army in southern Albania has gone over to the side of the people. We took Kalashnikovs away from the children. We're trying to organise and put together a true resistance. This is the only way we can face an attack from Berisha's forces."
Residents said they had seen an ageing Albanian air force MiG fighter on Wednesday evening firing into nearby mountains and at positions near the Vjose river running through the town.
Many men under arms said they believed an attack by Albanian troops was imminent.
Shops were empty, with residents systematically taking away anything left behind by their owners. Townsfolk said supplies had been halted by army roadblocks in Gjirokaster to the south.
"We have food shortages. I haven't seen bread for the past two days," said one elderly woman.
